propositions: Acceptance criteria must be classified as either codebase-verifiable (repository-detectable proof) or operator-attested (external evidence); the exact case-insensitive [operator-attested] tag selects operator attestation, while untagged or malformed tags default to codebase-verifiable.

Externally-verifiable criteria lacking the exact [operator-attested] tag or carrying malformed near-misses must produce findings that name the correct syntax; conversely, codebase-verifiable criteria incorrectly tagged [operator-attested] must be detected and reported as weaker than repository proof.
Criteria bundling both repository proof and outside-world proof must not be silently assigned one evidence kind; review must require the author to split them into independently certifiable criteria.

High-confidence evidence-classification mismatches must participate in normal validity × impact blocking policy and be validated against a frozen corpus with 100% precision on external negatives, 100% recall on known A1/115b/8c4f/malformed/over-tagged fixtures, and macro precision/recall ≥0.90.

The new criterion must be routed through the canonical registry, reviewer prompt and contract, criteria routing, generated criteria guide, and frozen evaluation corpus without drifting from ADR 0043 exact-tag semantics.

Deterministic keyword detection must remain advisory and fail-open, preserving execution outcomes (test runs, deployments, DB mutations) even when related implementation code exists and complements repository evidence.
